categories.name: Prompt Injection
categories.description: Adversary-controlled input that alters LLM behavior, bypasses safety controls, or coerces the model into unintended actions. Includes direct (user) and indirect (retrieved content, tool output) injection.

categories.name: Sensitive Information Disclosure
categories.description: LLM outputs leak PII, credentials, proprietary data, or system internals — via memorization of training data, retrieval of sensitive context, or leaky responses.

categories.name: Supply Chain
categories.description: Compromise via untrusted models, datasets, embeddings, plugins, or third-party fine-tunes. Includes typosquatted models on public hubs and tampered weights.

categories.name: Data and Model Poisoning
categories.description: Manipulation of pre-training, fine-tuning, or RAG data to introduce backdoors, biases, or vulnerabilities that surface at inference time.

categories.name: Improper Output Handling
categories.description: Insufficient validation of LLM outputs before they cross trust boundaries — leading to XSS, SSRF, SQLi, RCE when output is fed to browsers, shells, DBs, or downstream services.

categories.name: Excessive Agency
categories.description: LLM-driven systems with overbroad permissions, autonomy, or tool access. Includes too many tools, overly permissive functions, or autonomous actions without human gating.

categories.name: System Prompt Leakage
categories.description: Disclosure of system prompts revealing internal instructions, secrets, role boundaries, or business logic an attacker can exploit.

categories.name: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
categories.description: Risks in RAG pipelines: embedding inversion, cross-tenant data leakage in shared vector stores, retrieval poisoning, and access-control bypass via embeddings.

categories.name: Misinformation
categories.description: Hallucinated or fabricated outputs presented as factual — including fake citations, wrong code, and confident-but-wrong reasoning that drives downstream decisions.

categories.name: Unbounded Consumption
categories.description: Resource exhaustion attacks: token-flooding, model DoS, cost amplification (wallet drain), and runaway agentic loops.
